headline: Last session: Sensex fell 289 points, though Nifty and Sensex extended their weekly rally for a third week.

marketStatus.message: Market is closed today because it is a weekend. It will reopen on Monday, 16 November.

why: Inflation concerns weighed on sentiment during the last session, causing benchmark indices to slip.
Foreign fund inflows and lower crude oil prices supported market gains earlier in the week.
PSU Banks led sectoral gains, pushing Nifty50 and Sensex higher for the third consecutive week.
A mid-week surge added Rs 4.5 lakh crore in investor wealth with Sensex gaining over 1,200 points.
whatHappening: In the last trading session, Sensex fell 289 points as Nifty slipped.
Weekly market wrap showed NIFTY50 and SENSEX extending their rally for a third week.
Several major companies including Ashok Leyland, Powergrid, and PFC have upcoming corporate actions and dividend record dates.
GIFT Nifty signaled a weak opening ahead of Friday's trade.
summary: On the last trading day, Sensex declined by 289 points as inflation concerns weighed on the market. Despite the Friday dip, benchmark indices extended their weekly rally for a third consecutive week, led by PSU banks. Investors are focusing on upcoming corporate actions and dividend payouts for companies like Ashok Leyland, Powergrid, and PFC.
